<thought>The spectrum shows a monoisotopic peak at 114.07 with successive peaks spaced ~1 Da and decreasing intensities (≈6.7 %, 0.6 %, 0.03 %). This is the classic 13C isotopic envelope (M+1, M+2, …) indicating the presence of carbon. No characteristic Cl (M+2 ≈ 1/3 intensity), Br (M+2 ≈ 1 intensity), S, or other element patterns are observed. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution is carbon.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
